title: O God, Forsake Me Not
description: O God, Forsake Me Not in Tonic Solfa to WAS FRAG ICH NACH DER WELT, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Salomo Franck wrote these words in German. August Crull's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 347.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked 6.7.6.7.6.6.6.6, to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WAS FRAG ICH NACH DER WELT; any other 6.7.6.7.6.6.6.6 tune fits them as well.
underlay: O God, for-sake me not! Thy gra-cious pre-sence lend_ me; Lead Thou Thy help-less child, Thy Ho-ly Spir-it send_ me That I my course may run. Be Thou my Light, my Lot, My Staff, my Rock, my Shield,— O God, for-sake me not!

lines: That I my course may run.
Be Thou my Light, my Lot,
My Staff, my Rock, my Shield,—
Take not Thy Spirit from me
Be Thou my Strength and Power,—
And when the Prince of hell
Be Thou not far from me,—
Grant me true faith in Thee;
Grant that I leave Thee never;
When my good fight is fought,
Help me in life and death,—

licence: Public domain: Salomo Franck died in 1725; August Crull died in 1923.
credits: Words by Salomo Franck (1659–1725), translated by August Crull (1845–1923), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to WAS FRAG ICH NACH DER WELT by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
